newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt says to sell additional state shares.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt says to sell additional state shares.

text.p: The Czech government plans to sell shares it holds in reserve to cover potential restitution claims, Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux said on Wednesday.

He added at a weekly government news conference that the shares, which have a nominal value totalling 4.5 billion crowns, were from the country's most significant companies, but did not include those in the state-controlled Restitution Investment Fund.

"The government decided to release the so-far blocked reserves for restitution claims in individual companies with a total nominal value of 4.5 billion crowns, and these reserves in individual firms should be privatised," he said.
Lux said ministries with shares under their jurisdiction have been asked to submit privatisation plans for the strategic firms by March 15.
He said there were 53 firms currently listed as strategic by the government, with a total nominal value of 175 billion crowns.
Firms included on the list would be computer network firm PVT a.s., brewery Jihoceske Pivovary n.p., maker of the Czech Budweiser brand beer, and coal miner Zapadoceska Uhelna a.s..
He did not say which method the government would use to sell off the holdings.
"The government charged the ministers to submit a reassessment of the so-called strategic companies, of which there are 53...with the aim to put part of these companies into privatisation," Lux said.
"The will of the government is to reduce the number of strategic companies it holds," he added.
Lux said that the shares in the strategic companies was separate from the shares being sold from the restitution reserves.
